title: Singaporean Chilli Crab-Style Prawns
subtitle: King prawns in a spicy, tangy tomato and egg sauce
excerpt: Traditional Singaporean chilli crab uses whole mud crabs cooked in a sweet, spicy, and savoury tomato sauce thickened with beaten egg. King prawns make the dish accessible without specialist sourcing, and the sauce is just as good for mopping up with bread. This is one of the great dishes of Southeast Asian cooking.
sourceNotes: Chilli crab was created in Singapore in the 1950s by Cher Yam Tian, who began cooking crab with chilli and tomato sauce as a street food. It is now considered one of Singapore's national dishes.

content.text: Have everything prepared before the wok goes on. The sauce comes together in under 10 minutes and there is no time to prep during cooking.

items.prepNote: mixed with 2 tbsp cold water to make a slurry

content.text: Heat the wok over high heat until smoking. Add the sunflower oil, then the chilli paste, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the tinned tomatoes, fish sauce, palm sugar, and rice vinegar. Stir well and bring to a simmer.
Add the king prawns to the sauce and toss to coat. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the prawns are cooked through and have turned pink throughout.
Stir the cornflour slurry and pour it into the sauce. Stir for 1 minute until the sauce thickens.
Pour the beaten eggs slowly into the sauce in a thin stream while stirring. The egg should cook in ribbons through the sauce. Remove from the heat immediately.
Scatter the sliced spring onion over the top and serve with steamed rice or crusty bread for mopping up the sauce.

items.cause: The cornflour slurry was not stirred before adding, or not cooked for long enough
items.fix: Mix another small batch of cornflour slurry and stir it in. Simmer for another minute.

items.cause: Overcooked; prawns need only 4 to 5 minutes
items.fix: Remove the prawns as soon as they are uniformly pink and opaque. Return them to the finished sauce to serve.
